summary: The Western Area Power Administration moves to rescind the CAISO show cause order as to it. WAPA is a federal power marketing administration whose only CAISO-controlled asset is its share of the Path 15 Upgrade line.
ask: Rescind the June 18, 2026 show cause order against WAPA as a Participating Transmission Owner and waive any notice and comment periods.

points.point: WAPA placed only its Path 15 Upgrade Project interests under CAISO operational control, an 83-mile 500-kilovolt line.
points.quote: WAPA only placed under the operational control of the CAISO its rights and interests in the Path 15 Upgrade Project, a single, approximately 83-mile, 500-kilovolt transmission line

points.point: WAPA keeps the right to use its own tariff for interconnections to the Path 15 Upgrade where CAISO provisions are inconsistent.
points.quote: including use of its own Tarif or OATT for interconnections to the Path 15 Upgrade to the extent the CAISO provisions are inconsistent.

points.point: WAPA is exempt from FERC jurisdiction under FPA section 201(f) as a federal entity.
points.quote: WAPA is a non-public utility that is exempt from the Commission’s jurisdiction pursuant to Section 201(f) of the Federal Power Act.

points.point: WAPA will keep coordinating with CAISO and file tariff revisions if it finds changes are needed.
points.quote: WAPA will file proposed revisions to its Tariff with the Commission in due course.

throughLine.text: Uses the E-10 CAISO show cause order's offer to rescind the order against non-public utilities at their request. FERC granted this motion on August 14, 2026.
